title: The Image Stream: rapid serial images under a flash meter
acceptance: A stream of images replaces the retired flashing mode: frame replaces frame at 4 to 12 images per second, measured against WCAG 2.3.1 with at most two flashes in any second.

The first presenter is a fixation-aperture stream no larger than the safe area, free-running, behind its own build flag, with no reader able to reach it until the panel control and the photosensitivity notice land.
FLASHING_ENABLED stays false for the event economy; flashing-disabled.test.js keeps proving no reachable state flashes while the stream flag is off.

evidence.note: The proposal: the stream, the flash meter that measures light rather than counting events, the fixation aperture, and the order of work. The pure core is built on the branch.
The pure core: luminance summaries, the flash meter and the stream clock, with the spec. No surface is registered; nothing reaches a reader.
#721 merged: the pure core and the spec, before Codex's checkerboard finding was fixed.

The meter reads one cell per pixel and refuses coarser summaries: a checkerboard inverting at 12 Hz averaged to steady grey in the 24×24 grid and certified. Three tests written first, failing on main.
Branch image-stream-presenter: IMAGE_STREAM_ENABLED (off) and the surface stream registered behind it; flashing-disabled.test.js extended, image-stream-enabled.test.js added.

Branch image-stream-presenter: the fixation-aperture presenter (7cd92e42), its runtime meter and fail-closed stops (d5263b3b), and the wiring behind the flag: gated as a flash, mounted over Gallery, never handed to the visual engine.

Presenter: 140 px clamp, frame replaces frame, refresh measured, pause and seek, benign reel plays, strobe stopped within a second once the aperture outgrows the safe area, meter exceptions, stalls and settings stop it. Run in jsdom only; no real browser.
Step 2 as a draft pull request: the presenter, its runtime meter and the wiring, all behind IMAGE_STREAM_ENABLED (off).

activity.summary: Claimed: the pure core (luminance summaries, the flash meter, the stream clock) is built on image-stream-core; no surface is registered, so no reader can reach it.
PR #721 opened: the pure core and the spec
#721 merged as 31fbdeb2; PR #722 opened to fix the meter's coarse-grid blind spot
Step 2: the fixation-aperture presenter, behind IMAGE_STREAM_ENABLED (off)
PR #723 opened as a draft: the presenter behind its flag, held until Codex's findings are fixed

summary: A rapid serial stream of images beside the rapid serial stream of words: frames replacing frames at several per second, never passing through black, governed by the light it actually puts on the screen. The retired event economy limited risk by counting events, so this stream is measured against WCAG 2.3.1 instead, and FLASHING_ENABLED stays false.
